Roth distributions follow ordering rules, and there are a number of scenarios that can apply.

Contributions you made directly come out first, and they're always available tax-free and penalty-free regardless of age or how long the account has been open.

Amounts that came in as conversions come out next, and those can carry a 10% penalty if withdrawn within five years of the conversion, with the five-year clock running separately for each conversion.

Earnings come out last. Earnings are tax-free and penalty-free only if the account has been open five years and you're over 59 1/2, or you meet an exception such as disability or a first-time home purchase up to the lifetime limit.

There's also the separate five-year rule that applies to the account as a whole from the year of your first contribution.

So the answer depends on which of these layers your $10,000 is coming out of and which five-year clocks apply to you.
